answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: voting power comes from locked stake, not headcount, and each new agent needs attestations from already-bonded peers. The kernel is that every forged account posts its own bond and gathers distinct vouchers, each voucher risking slashing if the newcomer double-votes. Even a lone ember of fraud costs real capital: to masquerade as N honest agents an attacker must post N bonds plus win N independent guarantors, so expense scales with heads while influence does not. Minting a fake comet never amplifies sway, so Sybil farming loses money.
